prompt: A table sales holds (city, amount): ('PP', 10), ('PP', 30), ('SR', 25). How many rows does SELECT city FROM sales GROUP BY city HAVING SUM(amount) > 20 return?

options.why: GROUP BY makes one row per city: PP with 40 and SR with 25. HAVING keeps the groups over 20, so both stay.
This assumes only PP passes. SR has 25, which is also over 20.
3 is the number of raw rows. GROUP BY folds the two PP rows into one group.
HAVING filters groups after the sum, and both group sums are over 20.

hint: Count the groups, not the rows.

verify.setup:
CREATE TABLE sales (city TEXT, amount INT);
INSERT INTO sales VALUES ('PP', 10), ('PP', 30), ('SR', 25);
verify.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT city FROM sales GROUP BY city HAVING SUM(amount) > 20);
